It’s incredibly confusing and unsettling because even though I know no one is physically in the room with me, they sound just like actual people speaking.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there's anything unreal or not quite right about your perception of the world or yourself, or do you feel like everything makes sense and is as it should be, aside from the voices and your lack of motivation?\n\nPatient: Actually, there is something else that feels very off about how I perceive things. I've become convinced that the new standardized curriculum wasn't just about test scores, but was specifically designed to target me and make me look incompetent. My husband and coworkers keep telling me that this belief is irrational, but I just can't shake the feeling that it was made to set me up for failure.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about why you believe the new curriculum was specifically designed to target you, and what evidence you think supports this belief?\n\nPatient: It just feels so personal because the new rollout made me feel so incompetent, even though my husband and coworkers keep telling me that's irrational and everyone is struggling. I don't really have any proof, and the stress of it all has just left me feeling incredibly overwhelmed and exhausted by my daily teaching workload.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you is something that might be influenced by your current low mood and lack of motivation, or do you firmly believe it's a fact regardless of how you're feeling?\n\nPatient: I firmly believe it is a fact regardless of how I am feeling. Even though my husband and coworkers insist it is just a general change and that my belief is irrational, in my heart I still feel absolutely certain it was designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It feels like an undeniable reality to me, not just a result of my low mood.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other explanation, no matter how small, for why the new curriculum might have been implemented, or are you completely convinced it was designed specifically to target you?\n\nPatient: I know my husband and colleagues keep telling me that the curriculum is just about standardized test scores and that everyone is struggling with it. But despite what they say, I still feel deeply convinced in my heart that it was designed specifically to target me and make me look incompetent. I just find it really hard to see it any other way.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation or event where your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you was challenged by someone you trust, and how you responded to their perspective?\n\nPatient: My husband sat me down recently and showed me district-wide emails to prove that every teacher is facing these exact same curriculum changes, not just me. Although I trust him and logically know he is trying to help, I still feel deeply convinced that the changes were secretly designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It leaves me feeling really conflicted because I just can't fully accept his reassurance.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of motivation and interest in activities is directly related to the voices you hear and your belief that the curriculum is targeting you, or are these separate issues for you?\n\nPatient: They actually feel like somewhat separate issues to me, mostly because of the timing. It is just incredibly difficult to shake this feeling or see it any other way, even though I know others disagree with my perspective. Honestly, it feels pretty unshakeable to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your conviction that the curriculum is targeting you affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief influences your relationships or overall well-being?\n\nPatient: Believing that the curriculum is targeting me has made me feel incredibly defensive and isolated, especially since my husband and coworkers keep telling me I'm being irrational, which just makes me feel misunderstood. This constant worry has caused me to pull away from school committees, social gatherings, and theater because I feel too overwhelmed and anxious to engage with anyone normally. It has really strained my relationships and left me feeling completely cut off from the people who support me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your conviction that the curriculum is targeting you is something that could potentially change if you started feeling better about yourself and your teaching, or do you believe it's a fact that will remain true regardless of your mood or circumstances?"

They feed right into my worst fears of failing my students, even though I logically know there is no one physically in the room saying those things to me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the critical voices you hear are related to your own thoughts or do you believe they are coming from an external source that is trying to tell you something about your teaching?\n\nPatient: They definitely sound like real, distinct voices coming from outside of my head, rather than just my own thoughts. It’s incredibly confusing and unsettling because even though I know no one is physically in the room with me, they sound just like actual people speaking.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there's anything unreal or not quite right about your perception of the world or yourself, or do you feel like everything makes sense and is as it should be, aside from the voices and your lack of motivation?\n\nPatient: Actually, there is something else that feels very off about how I perceive things. I've become convinced that the new standardized curriculum wasn't just about test scores, but was specifically designed to target me and make me look incompetent. My husband and coworkers keep telling me that this belief is irrational, but I just can't shake the feeling that it was made to set me up for failure.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about why you believe the new curriculum was specifically designed to target you, and what evidence you think supports this belief?\n\nPatient: It just feels so personal because the new rollout made me feel so incompetent, even though my husband and coworkers keep telling me that's irrational and everyone is struggling. I don't really have any proof, and the stress of it all has just left me feeling incredibly overwhelmed and exhausted by my daily teaching workload.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you is something that might be influenced by your current low mood and lack of motivation, or do you firmly believe it's a fact regardless of how you're feeling?\n\nPatient: I firmly believe it is a fact regardless of how I am feeling. Even though my husband and coworkers insist it is just a general change and that my belief is irrational, in my heart I still feel absolutely certain it was designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It feels like an undeniable reality to me, not just a result of my low mood.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other explanation, no matter how small, for why the new curriculum might have been implemented, or are you completely convinced it was designed specifically to target you?\n\nPatient: I know my husband and colleagues keep telling me that the curriculum is just about standardized test scores and that everyone is struggling with it. I just find it really hard to see it any other way.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation or event where your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you was challenged by someone you trust, and how you responded to their perspective?\n\nPatient: My husband sat me down recently and showed me district-wide emails to prove that every teacher is facing these exact same curriculum changes, not just me. The voices criticizing me and the feeling that the curriculum is targeting me only began a few months ago, late in the last semester.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or circumstance under which you might consider the possibility that your belief about the curriculum targeting you could be incorrect, or is this belief unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: While my husband and coworkers keep telling me my belief is irrational and that everyone is facing the same changes, it still feels deeply personal and targeted specifically at me. It feels like an objective reality to me, not something tied to my self-esteem.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of motivation and interest in activities is a result of the voices and your beliefs about the curriculum, or are these issues separate from each other?\n\nPatient: They actually feel like separate issues to me because the timing is so different. The lack of motivation and loss of interest started a little over a year ago when the new curriculum was first rolled out. The voices and the belief that I am being targeted only started a few months ago, so the loss of drive was already happening long before those other things began.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your beliefs about the curriculum targeting you and the voices you hear could be related to your own thoughts and feelings, rather than being based on actual events or external forces?"

I don't really have any proof, and the stress of it all has just left me feeling incredibly overwhelmed and exhausted by my daily teaching workload.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you is something that might be influenced by your current low mood and lack of motivation, or do you firmly believe it's a fact regardless of how you're feeling?\n\nPatient: I firmly believe it is a fact regardless of how I am feeling. Even though my husband and coworkers insist it is just a general change and that my belief is irrational, in my heart I still feel absolutely certain it was designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It feels like an undeniable reality to me, not just a result of my low mood.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other explanation, no matter how small, for why the new curriculum might have been implemented, or are you completely convinced it was designed specifically to target you?\n\nPatient: I know my husband and colleagues keep telling me that the curriculum is just about standardized test scores and that everyone is struggling with it. But despite what they say, I still feel deeply convinced in my heart that it was designed specifically to target me and make me look incompetent. I just find it really hard to see it any other way.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation or event where your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you was challenged by someone you trust, and how you responded to their perspective?\n\nPatient: My husband sat me down recently and showed me district-wide emails to prove that every teacher is facing these exact same curriculum changes, not just me. Although I trust him and logically know he is trying to help, I still feel deeply convinced that the changes were secretly designed to target me and make me look incompetent. The lack of motivation and losing my spark for teaching and theater started a little over a year ago. The voices criticizing me and the feeling that the curriculum is targeting me only began a few months ago, late in the last semester.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or circumstance under which you might consider the possibility that your belief about the curriculum targeting you could be incorrect, or is this belief unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: While my husband and coworkers keep telling me my belief is irrational and that everyone is facing the same changes, it still feels deeply personal and targeted specifically at me. It is just incredibly difficult to shake this feeling or see it any other way, even though I know others disagree with my perspective. Honestly, it feels pretty unshakeable to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your conviction that the curriculum is targeting you affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief influences your relationships or overall well-being?\n\nPatient: Believing that the curriculum is targeting me has made me feel incredibly defensive and isolated, especially since my husband and coworkers keep telling me I'm being irrational, which just makes me feel misunderstood. To me, they just feel like separate, overwhelming things that I'm dealing with. I'm honestly not sure if one is causing the other.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or events that would make you question or change your belief that the curriculum is targeting you, or is this belief absolute for you?"

My husband and coworkers have tried to reassure me that these changes affect everyone and that my belief is irrational, but it still feels deeply real and hard to question. Despite all of their logical arguments, the feeling that I am being specifically targeted feels almost absolute to me.

I can't find the motivation or pleasure to start anything, even though I know my career and hobbies are slipping away.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced episodes like this before in your life, where you felt a significant loss of interest and drive, or is this the first time you've felt this way for such an extended period?\n\nPatient: No, this is the first time I've ever felt like this in my life. I've always successfully managed my busy schedule of teaching, coaching, and theater in the past, but this loss of drive and interest only started building about 14 months ago.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned this is the first time you've felt this way for such an extended period, but can you tell me if you've had any periods over the past 14 months where your motivation and interest in activities returned to normal, even if only for a short time?\n\nPatient: No, there haven't been any breaks or times where my motivation returned to normal. It has been a continuous, steady decline since the curriculum rollout, and it's actually only gotten worse over the past 14 months. I haven't had a single day where I felt like my usual energetic self.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any periods of significant improvement or normal mood and motivation that lasted for at least two months during these 14 months, or has it been a consistent decline without any notable improvements?\n\nPatient: No, there haven't been any periods of improvement or normal motivation at all, let alone for two months. It has been a completely consistent, gradual decline since the new curriculum was rolled out. I haven't had any breaks where I felt like my old self.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned a steady decline over 14 months without any periods of improvement, but can you clarify if there have been any subtle fluctuations in your symptoms, such as slight improvements or worsenings, in response to specific events or circumstances?\n\nPatient: There haven't been any periods of improvement; it has really just felt like a continuous downward slide. However, things did take a distinct turn for the worse a few months ago, towards the stressful end of the last semester, when I started hearing those critical voices and feeling like the new curriculum was specifically targeting me.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned hearing critical voices a few months ago, can you tell me more about what you mean by that, such as what the voices say and how often you hear them?\n\nPatient: When I'm alone in my classroom after school, I hear a male and a female voice commenting on my teaching, saying things like, \"She's failing them.\" This has been happening for the last few months, since late last semester. Even though I know there is no one actually in the room with me, hearing those voices feels incredibly real and distressing.\n\nDoctor: Have the voices you've been hearing ever told you to do anything, or are they just commenting on your actions or situation?\n\nPatient: No, they don't tell me to do anything. They just comment on my actions, specifically criticizing my teaching by saying things like \"She's failing them\" when I'm alone in my classroom after school.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, besides hearing the critical voices?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't seen anything unusual or experienced any other kinds of hallucinations. It is really just those two voices commenting on my teaching when I'm alone in my classroom.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the comments from the voices are true, or do you think they are just critical and not based on reality?\n\nPatient: Because my teaching performance has actually declined so much and I've been struggling to keep up, those comments feel painfully true. They feed right into my worst fears of failing my students, even though I logically know there is no one physically in the room saying those things to me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the critical voices you hear are related to your own thoughts or do you believe they are coming from an external source that is trying to tell you something about your teaching?\n\nPatient: They definitely sound like real, distinct voices coming from outside of my head, rather than just my own thoughts. It’s incredibly confusing and unsettling because even though I know no one is physically in the room with me, they sound just like actual people speaking.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there's anything unreal or not quite right about your perception of the world or yourself, or do you feel like everything makes sense and is as it should be, aside from the voices and your lack of motivation?\n\nPatient: Actually, there is something else that feels very off about how I perceive things. I've become convinced that the new standardized curriculum wasn't just about test scores, but was specifically designed to target me and make me look incompetent. My husband and coworkers keep telling me that this belief is irrational, but I just can't shake the feeling that it was made to set me up for failure.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about why you believe the new curriculum was specifically designed to target you, and what evidence you think supports this belief?\n\nPatient: It just feels so personal because the new rollout made me feel so incompetent, even though my husband and coworkers keep telling me that's irrational and everyone is struggling. I don't really have any proof, and the stress of it all has just left me feeling incredibly overwhelmed and exhausted by my daily teaching workload.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you is something that might be influenced by your current low mood and lack of motivation, or do you firmly believe it's a fact regardless of how you're feeling?\n\nPatient: I firmly believe it is a fact regardless of how I am feeling. Even though my husband and coworkers insist it is just a general change and that my belief is irrational, in my heart I still feel absolutely certain it was designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It feels like an undeniable reality to me, not just a result of my low mood.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other explanation, no matter how small, for why the new curriculum might have been implemented, or are you completely convinced it was designed specifically to target you?\n\nPatient: I know my husband and colleagues keep telling me that the curriculum is just about standardized test scores and that everyone is struggling with it. But despite what they say, I still feel deeply convinced in my heart that it was designed specifically to target me and make me look incompetent. I just find it really hard to see it any other way.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation or event where your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you was challenged by someone you trust, and how you responded to their perspective?\n\nPatient: My husband sat me down recently and showed me district-wide emails to prove that every teacher is facing these exact same curriculum changes, not just me. Although I trust him and logically know he is trying to help, I still feel deeply convinced that the changes were secretly designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It leaves me feeling really conflicted because I just can't fully accept his reassurance.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of motivation and interest in activities is directly related to the voices you hear and your belief that the curriculum is targeting you, or are these separate issues for you?\n\nPatient: They actually feel like somewhat separate issues to me, mostly because of the timing. The lack of motivation and losing my spark for teaching and theater started a little over a year ago. The voices criticizing me and the feeling that the curriculum is targeting me only began a few months ago, late in the last semester.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or circumstance under which you might consider the possibility that your belief about the curriculum targeting you could be incorrect, or is this belief unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: While my husband and coworkers keep telling me my belief is irrational and that everyone is facing the same changes, it still feels deeply personal and targeted specifically at me. It is just incredibly difficult to shake this feeling or see it any other way, even though I know others disagree with my perspective. Honestly, it feels pretty unshakeable to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your conviction that the curriculum is targeting you affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief influences your relationships or overall well-being?\n\nPatient: Believing that the curriculum is targeting me has made me feel incredibly defensive and isolated, especially since my husband and coworkers keep telling me I'm being irrational, which just makes me feel misunderstood. This constant worry has caused me to pull away from school committees, social gatherings, and theater because I feel too overwhelmed and anxious to engage with anyone normally. It has really strained my relationships and left me feeling completely cut off from the people who support me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your conviction that the curriculum is targeting you is something that could potentially change if you started feeling better about yourself and your teaching, or do you believe it's a fact that will remain true regardless of your mood or circumstances?\n\nPatient: I believe it is a fact that will remain true regardless of how I feel. Even if my mood improved or I felt better about my teaching, I would still believe the curriculum was intentionally designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It feels like an objective reality to me, not something tied to my self-esteem.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of motivation and interest in activities is a result of the voices and your beliefs about the curriculum, or are these issues separate from each other?\n\nPatient: They actually feel like separate issues to me because the timing is so different. The lack of motivation and loss of interest started a little over a year ago when the new curriculum was first rolled out. The voices and the belief that I am being targeted only started a few months ago, so the loss of drive was already happening long before those other things began.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your beliefs about the curriculum targeting you and the voices you hear could be related to your own thoughts and feelings, rather than being based on actual events or external forces?\n\nPatient: A part of me knows it sounds irrational, since my husband says everyone is facing the same changes and I know no one is physically in the classroom with me. But when it's happening, the voices and the feeling of being targeted feel so incredibly real and personal. It makes it very hard for me to completely dismiss them as just my own thoughts.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of motivation and interest in activities could be contributing to your beliefs about the curriculum targeting you, or do you believe these are completely separate issues?\n\nPatient: I haven't really thought about whether my lack of motivation and my beliefs about the curriculum are connected. To me, they just feel like separate, overwhelming things that I'm dealing with. I'm honestly not sure if one is causing the other.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or events that would make you question or change your belief that the curriculum is targeting you, or is this belief absolute for you?\n\nPatient: My husband and coworkers have tried to reassure me that these changes affect everyone and that my belief is irrational, but it still feels deeply real and hard to question. Despite all of their logical arguments, the feeling that I am being specifically targeted feels almost absolute to me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voices and your belief about the curriculum targeting you would go away if you were able to regain your motivation and interest in teaching and theater, or do you think these issues are completely unrelated?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure if they are related, or if one would go away if the other improved. It all just feels like a confusing, overwhelming mess that started during the same difficult period of my life. Because of that, I haven't really thought about how they might connect.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of motivation and interest in activities is more distressing to you, or is it the voices and the belief that the curriculum is targeting you that causes you more distress?"

They just comment on my actions, specifically criticizing my teaching by saying things like \"She's failing them\" when I'm alone in my classroom after school.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, besides hearing the critical voices?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't seen anything unusual or experienced any other kinds of hallucinations. It is really just those two voices commenting on my teaching when I'm alone in my classroom.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the comments from the voices are true, or do you think they are just critical and not based on reality?\n\nPatient: Because my teaching performance has actually declined so much and I've been struggling to keep up, those comments feel painfully true. They feed right into my worst fears of failing my students, even though I logically know there is no one physically in the room saying those things to me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the critical voices you hear are related to your own thoughts or do you believe they are coming from an external source that is trying to tell you something about your teaching?\n\nPatient: They definitely sound like real, distinct voices coming from outside of my head, rather than just my own thoughts. It’s incredibly confusing and unsettling because even though I know no one is physically in the room with me, they sound just like actual people speaking.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there's anything unreal or not quite right about your perception of the world or yourself, or do you feel like everything makes sense and is as it should be, aside from the voices and your lack of motivation?\n\nPatient: Actually, there is something else that feels very off about how I perceive things. I've become convinced that the new standardized curriculum wasn't just about test scores, but was specifically designed to target me and make me look incompetent. My husband and coworkers keep telling me that this belief is irrational, but I just can't shake the feeling that it was made to set me up for failure.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about why you believe the new curriculum was specifically designed to target you, and what evidence you think supports this belief?\n\nPatient: It just feels so personal because the new rollout made me feel so incompetent, even though my husband and coworkers keep telling me that's irrational and everyone is struggling. I don't really have any proof, and the stress of it all has just left me feeling incredibly overwhelmed and exhausted by my daily teaching workload.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you is something that might be influenced by your current low mood and lack of motivation, or do you firmly believe it's a fact regardless of how you're feeling?\n\nPatient: I firmly believe it is a fact regardless of how I am feeling. Even though my husband and coworkers insist it is just a general change and that my belief is irrational, in my heart I still feel absolutely certain it was designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It feels like an undeniable reality to me, not just a result of my low mood.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other explanation, no matter how small, for why the new curriculum might have been implemented, or are you completely convinced it was designed specifically to target you?\n\nPatient: I know my husband and colleagues keep telling me that the curriculum is just about standardized test scores and that everyone is struggling with it. But despite what they say, I still feel deeply convinced in my heart that it was designed specifically to target me and make me look incompetent. I just find it really hard to see it any other way.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation or event where your belief that the curriculum was designed to target you was challenged by someone you trust, and how you responded to their perspective?\n\nPatient: My husband sat me down recently and showed me district-wide emails to prove that every teacher is facing these exact same curriculum changes, not just me. Although I trust him and logically know he is trying to help, I still feel deeply convinced that the changes were secretly designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It leaves me feeling really conflicted because I just can't fully accept his reassurance.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of motivation and interest in activities is directly related to the voices you hear and your belief that the curriculum is targeting you, or are these separate issues for you?\n\nPatient: They actually feel like somewhat separate issues to me, mostly because of the timing. The lack of motivation and losing my spark for teaching and theater started a little over a year ago. The voices criticizing me and the feeling that the curriculum is targeting me only began a few months ago, late in the last semester.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or circumstance under which you might consider the possibility that your belief about the curriculum targeting you could be incorrect, or is this belief unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: While my husband and coworkers keep telling me my belief is irrational and that everyone is facing the same changes, it still feels deeply personal and targeted specifically at me. It is just incredibly difficult to shake this feeling or see it any other way, even though I know others disagree with my perspective. Honestly, it feels pretty unshakeable to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your conviction that the curriculum is targeting you affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief influences your relationships or overall well-being?\n\nPatient: Believing that the curriculum is targeting me has made me feel incredibly defensive and isolated, especially since my husband and coworkers keep telling me I'm being irrational, which just makes me feel misunderstood. This constant worry has caused me to pull away from school committees, social gatherings, and theater because I feel too overwhelmed and anxious to engage with anyone normally. It has really strained my relationships and left me feeling completely cut off from the people who support me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your conviction that the curriculum is targeting you is something that could potentially change if you started feeling better about yourself and your teaching, or do you believe it's a fact that will remain true regardless of your mood or circumstances?\n\nPatient: I believe it is a fact that will remain true regardless of how I feel. Even if my mood improved or I felt better about my teaching, I would still believe the curriculum was intentionally designed to target me and make me look incompetent. It feels like an objective reality to me, not something tied to my self-esteem.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of motivation and interest in activities is a result of the voices and your beliefs about the curriculum, or are these issues separate from each other?\n\nPatient: They actually feel like separate issues to me because the timing is so different. The lack of motivation and loss of interest started a little over a year ago when the new curriculum was first rolled out. The voices and the belief that I am being targeted only started a few months ago, so the loss of drive was already happening long before those other things began.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your beliefs about the curriculum targeting you and the voices you hear could be related to your own thoughts and feelings, rather than being based on actual events or external forces?\n\nPatient: A part of me knows it sounds irrational, since my husband says everyone is facing the same changes and I know no one is physically in the classroom with me. But when it's happening, the voices and the feeling of being targeted feel so incredibly real and personal. It makes it very hard for me to completely dismiss them as just my own thoughts.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of motivation and interest in activities could be contributing to your beliefs about the curriculum targeting you, or do you believe these are completely separate issues?\n\nPatient: I haven't really thought about whether my lack of motivation and my beliefs about the curriculum are connected. To me, they just feel like separate, overwhelming things that I'm dealing with. I'm honestly not sure if one is causing the other.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or events that would make you question or change your belief that the curriculum is targeting you, or is this belief absolute for you?\n\nPatient: My husband and coworkers have tried to reassure me that these changes affect everyone and that my belief is irrational, but it still feels deeply real and hard to question. Despite all of their logical arguments, the feeling that I am being specifically targeted feels almost absolute to me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voices and your belief about the curriculum targeting you would go away if you were able to regain your motivation and interest in teaching and theater, or do you think these issues are completely unrelated?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure if they are related, or if one would go away if the other improved. It all just feels like a confusing, overwhelming mess that started during the same difficult period of my life. Ultimately, while the paranoia is more frightening, losing my \"spark\" is the most profoundly depressing because it feels like I've lost who I am."
